MEETING HEADER
Date: 2025-10-29 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 90m
Attendees: Lena Park (AE), Marco Diaz (SE), Priya Nair (SE), Alex Johnson (West AE), Samira Patel (Field SE), Tom Brooks (Field AE), plus a few observers
Recording id: ff-20251029-lssd-0047

SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Run three demo scenarios (PLG quick win, enterprise migration, on-prem compliance).
- Focus on competitive positioning vs OpenAI/Anthropic and on dedicated/private talking points.
- Action items: update playbook, record demo snippets, schedule follow-ups.

TOPICS COVERED:
- Messaging frameworks (problem->solution->proof)
- Demo cheats (what to show first, what to hide)
- Handling pricing objections and latency vs cost
- Dedicated vs hosted vs private deployment tradeoffs
- Security compliance talking points (SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs)

[00:00] Lena (AE): All right everyone, thanks for joining. This is the "live sandtable" scrimmage — quick, kinda messy, practice firing. We'll run three 15-minute roleplays with feedback. Um, Marco you'll be playing the customer engineer on round one, Alex you'll take objections round two, Samira you'll do the VPC/privates question. Sound good?

[00:22] Marco (SE): Yep. Quick note, I'm gonna intentionally bring up the usual stuff — "how do you compare to OpenAI pricing", "what about Anthropic safety", that kind of thing.

[00:30] Alex (AE): And I'll pepper in procurement questions — legal, SOC, SSO — make it as realistic as possible.

[00:35] Tom (Field AE): Cool. I wanna focus on the latency/cost play too, we get that a lot — customers say they want sub-50ms but don't want to pay premium.

[00:44] Priya (SE): Great. Okay first scenario: "PLG startup wants to add chat summaries and embeddings for search, cost sensitive, wants hosted API but may go dedicated later." Marco, you start as the customer.

[00:55] Marco as Customer: Hi, hey, um, we currently use the other guys and we're seeing token spikes. How do y'all manage cost? And is your hosted API actually cheaper than self-hosting?

[01:10] Lena (AE): Yeah good — so we frame it that hosted is fastest to get going, we do model variants and automatic prefix caching so common queries are cheap. For unit economics we point to the Optimize toolkit — suggestions for batching and quantization, and we have example configs that typically lower per-token cost by 20-40% depending on the workload.

[01:32] Marco as Customer: Quantiza-tion? Like you do quantize-ization automatically?

[01:37] Priya (SE): (laughs) We recommend quant profiles — not always automatic, it's model and workload dependent. For many customers we recommend int8 or semi-quant modes and our runtime picks kernels to keep latency stable.

[01:50] Alex (AE): Quick objection: "what about hallucination risk if you compress models too much?"

[01:56] Marco as Customer: Yes, that's a fear.

[02:00] Priya (SE): Great question — we tie quantization suggestions to evals. Our Optimize has prompt sets and automatic QA runs; if quality drops we revert to a higher-precision variant. So it's not blind. Also we recommend keeping critical paths on a higher-precision model and using quantized variants for bulk throughput.

[02:20] Tom (Field AE): That's the demo nugget — show the metrics: throughput up, cost down, and no regression on the eval set.

[02:28] Lena (AE): Nice. Feedback on that round: good callouts on evals, Marco, but try to press harder on "what's the migration path" — customers like a clear timeline from hosted to dedicated.

[02:40] Marco (SE): Noted. Round two: enterprise migration scenario — Alex, you're the director of AI platform.

[02:47] Alex as Director: We're regulated, we need audit logs, SSO, and we might need VPC. Can Redwood run in our VPC or on-prem?

[02:56] Priya (SE): Short answer: yes. We have Redwood Private — VPC and on-prem options. For VPC we offer a private control plane plus customer-managed network peering; on-prem is a packaged deploy. Key management with KMS/HSM integrations supported, and audit logs are shipped to your SIEM or retained in our platform per the compliance package.

[03:20] Alex as Director: And SOC2? We need that for procurement.

[03:24] Marco (SE): Redwood is SOC 2 Type II — we have reports — SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC controls, and per-route audit trails.

[03:33] Alex as Director: How about data residency? We have EU customers.

[03:36] Priya (SE): We can pin region and provide EU-only deployments under the private offering; hosted also supports regional isolation but for strict residency we recommend Private.

[03:46] Alex as Director: Price delta between hosted and dedicated?

[03:50] Lena (AE): Hosted pricing is usage-based (tokens/embeds). Dedicated is reserved capacity commitments — typically better for predictable throughput; unit price per token can be lower once committed, but there's a platform/reservation fee. We usually show customers a 12-month TCO comparison.

[04:05] Marco (SE): From a SE perspective, emphasize predictable latency SLOs on Dedicated and the autoscale/burst policies — customers like the downtime protections.

[04:15] Samira (Field SE): Quick nit: people confuse "dedicated" with "on-prem" — call out differences: Dedicated is our reserved GPU pools managed by Redwood; on-prem means customer-managed infra.

[04:28] Lena (AE): Yep. Good call.

[04:32] Timestamp jump — move to scenario three: technical deep dive on fallback strategies. Samira, you want to be the skeptical customer.

[04:42] Samira as Customer: We're worried about failover — if your primary model is down or capacity hits, what's the app behavior?

[04:48] Priya (SE): We have smart routing and automatic fallback: policy-based routing by latency, cost, and region. You can configure automatic fallback to a compatible variant (smaller model or quantized) when capacity is low. We'll demo streaming + fallback in the recorded clip.

[05:05] Marco as Customer: Does that mean context or the K-V cache is preserved on fallback?

[05:10] Priya (SE): Good call — K-V cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash) isn't magically shared across incompatible model families. For compatible variants we preserve KV state; for variant switching we replay session up to a safe window. This is why model compatibility mapping is important.

[05:30] Tom (Field AE): Add that to the talking points — "KV cache preservation depends on compatibility; we fall back only to compatible variants to avoid hallucination." Short phrase: "fallback without fuzz." (laughter)

[05:45] Lena (AE): Okay mid-call check. A few common tough objections we didn't cover: "Why not use OpenAI — they have scale"; "We can self-host cheaper"; and "Anthropic sells safety". Let's roleplay "why OpenAI" quick.

[05:58] Marco as Customer: OpenAI gives us excellent developer ergonomics and fast time-to-market — why choose Redwood?

[06:06] Priya (SE): We lean on three pillars: production economics (controls for cost/latency), deployment flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private), and observability/ops (per-route tracing, token-level cost). For teams that outgrow a single provider, we offer migration paths and consistent APIs across environments.

[06:25] Alex (AE): Also call out judgeable differentiators: first-class batching and caching, kernel selection for low-latency on commodity GPUs, and model variance drop-in without app-level changes.

[06:40] Samira (Field SE): On the "self-host" objection, demo the hidden ops cost: orchestration, kernel tuning, 24/7 reliability, and fallback plumbing. Customers often underestimate the engineering effort.

[06:53] Marco as Customer: But what about price? If we commit, can we beat OpenAI per-token?

[06:58] Lena (AE): It depends. For long-running high throughput workloads, Dedicated reserved capacity typically lowers unit cost; hosted remains great for fast iteration. We present a 12-month comparative spreadsheet to procurement that shows break-even points.

[07:14] Side note: someone (transcription says "SageOS") — likely misheard — we should add Mistral/Cohere into the competitive slides.

[07:22] Feedback loop: After each roleplay, we paused for critique. Notes were: be explicit about fallback caveats, quantization tradeoffs, and call out the Optimize recommendations as a prescriptive checklist.

[07:38] Marco (SE): Quick practice on the demo flow: start with a simple prompt, show streaming tokens, then show a rare long-tail query hitting the fallback and show latency/quality tradeoff metrics. Keep each demo segment under 90s.

[07:55] Priya (SE): Yeah, and for security buyers, show the audit log sample and the SAML user provisioning flow — quick 30s clip.

[08:05] Alex (AE): Also practice an answer for "what if we require private cloud with HSM" — short answer: supported via Private with KMS/HSM integration and we can run under their key material.

[08:19] Tom (Field AE): There was a good interruption: "what's the timeline to go from hosted to dedicated - we don't want a migration that takes months." Typical is 2-6 weeks depending on model size and validation; we should put an expected timeline in the playbook.

[08:33] Lena (AE): Agreed. We'll add a timeline matrix to the playbook — small models quick, large models + regulated customers need more validation.

[08:40] (break — 5 mins) — attendees discuss slides

[13:40] Back from break — rapid-fire objections practice. Alex simulates procurement: "We need UNLIMITED audit logs" form question.

[13:55] Priya (SE): We offer extended retention as an add-on; if they need unbounded retention we work with infra to route logs to their SIEM.

[14:05] Marco (SE): Good — don't say "we can" without a clear handoff. Offer a next step: run playbook for their retention needs and get engineering alignment.

[14:12] Exercise: Demo speed run. Marco times Priya doing a demo. Priya standard flow: quick intro, launch sample prompt, show streaming, show token-level cost breakdown in console, compare to a quantized variant.

[14:40] (transcription glitch: "token-levil" instead of token-level)

[15:00] Priya (SE): And close with next step: we'll propose a pilot — 30 days with a capped spend, a few success metrics: latency P95, cost per 1000 tokens, and quality regression threshold.

[15:20] Alex (AE): Perfect. For the playbook, let's enumerate the success criteria we commonly ask for: latency target, cost threshold, regulatory constraints, timeline, and internal champions.

[15:35] Tom (Field AE): Also include a "who to loop in" checklist — e.g., platform, procurement, security, infra owners, legal.

[15:45] Final coaching round — rapid feedback: keep the demo lean, call out the migration path early, be explicit on tradeoffs, and use bench numbers (links: drive.com/benchmarks-v2 — note: placeholder link) not just claims.

[16:05] Lena (AE) - RECAP: solid practice. Action items — Marco will update the deck and the objection playbook (deadline 2025-11-05). Priya will capture two 60s demo clips: streaming + fallback and SAML provisioning (deadline 2025-11-03). I'll schedule two follow-up scrimmages in the next two weeks and send invites.

[16:25] Quick questions from observers: "Can we add a snippet for 'edge' use cases?" Marco: yes, add a one-pager on edge latency/quantization.

[16:38] Closing comments: keep practicing with the roleplay forms in the playbook. Lena: shout out — good energy, keep refining the canned rebuttals.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
